A narrower case survives: a target she renamed

trigger this check at all, since no call
mentions it. The consequence is mild, though:
it simply gets graded, and prompts do not
depend on matching anything in results.json.

Student source code is no longer stored here:
it stays on the autograder container and is
read from disk when building a prompt. What
this schema does hold is student identifiers
and the AI feedback written about their work.
In IMMEDIATE mode their code still reaches a
third-party LLM within seconds of submission,
it just is not retained by us. Privacy,
retention and consent remain out of scope in
the SRS, which is fine for a design document
and not for a live course.
Functional test outcomes are no longer stored.
results.json carries them to the student, and
the AI phase parses them to build prompts, but
That leaves FR-8, FR-9 and FR-10 partly

deductions" can only be derived from AI scores.
